captions.text: Something far away has noticed you.

notes: A slow push-in from high above the lone Wanderer settles behind their shoulder, locking eyes with the distant beacon.

action: You use your new ability to notice things and find your magical cape and hat from your memory bag. you launch yourself into the sky and float toward distant beacon with caution, you bring out your magic wand as you approach in case you need it.

ruling: The cape and hat answer the Wanderer's memory and lift them into the air, and this first act of magic awakens Mana (40/60). Flight is not free: it costs 15 as the cape drinks deeply, leaving 25. The wand is drawn and ready, but the miss means the plain does not let them approach unnoticed. The beacon doesn't grow closer as it should, and the mist below turns to rings of blue light that all point toward the Wanderer. The beacon has noticed them, and a clock of its attention ticks. The Wanderer is still aloft and unharmed, but the wand hums nervously and the light now pulses once, like a slow answer.

roll.presentation: An unseen hand: the glassy plain answers the flight with a hidden omen.
roll.reason: Whether the flight toward the unknown beacon goes unnoticed and cheap (cautious +1)

ops.label: Mana
ops.rules: Flight with the cape costs about 10-15 per leg; the wand's spells cost 10-30; regain 10 by resting on the plain, more at sources of light.

ops.label: The Beacon's Gaze
ops.rules: Ticks when the Wanderer uses magic carelessly or fails near the beacon; at 6 the beacon acts. Lowers with stealth or offerings.

narration: The cape unfurls from your memory like a held breath released, and the hat settles warm against your brow. You rise, and the plain falls away beneath you. Mana floods in, bright and cold, then drains as the cape drinks deep, leaving you thinner than you began. The wand hums in your fist. Yet the beacon does not grow nearer. Below, the mist gathers into rings of blue light, every ring tilting toward you like a thousand turning eyes. Far north, the white light pulses once, slow and deliberate, like an answer to a question you never asked.
movement: Rises about 20 m into the air and drifts north roughly 10 m, but the beacon stays the same distance away; the Wanderer hovers aloft.

facts.description: A long midnight-blue cape lined with faintly glowing silver thread streams behind the Wanderer, and a tall soft pointed hat sits on their head. The wand in their right hand is slender, pale wood tipped with a small trembling spark of light.

facts.description: A single steady white light, sharp as a lantern, low on the horizon. It now pulses once in a slow, deliberate rhythm, and a long bright reflection runs down the glassy plain toward the Wanderer. It does not seem to get closer, however far the Wanderer flies.
facts.placement: About 2 km due north of the Wanderer, at ground level on the horizon.

notes: I gave the Wanderer a streaming midnight cape with silver-thread lining, a tall soft hat and a sparking wand, and lifted them 20 m up. Below, pale blue rings in the mist converge on the point beneath them and pulse together.

cutscene.title: The Answering Light
cutscene.style: One slow orbit-and-settle move: rings of blue watch from below as the beacon pulses once, ending behind the Wanderer's shoulder.

notes: A slow pull-back from the Wanderer reveals the blue rings turning toward them, then settles behind the cape facing the unreachable beacon.

action: You can barely see anything in the distant, there must be something there, perhaps a portal to another world. You squint your eyes so that you can see more detail and approach, it's working you can start to see something, what is it, the floor is swirling, an asteroid crashes in the distance.

ruling: Partial hit (5 +2 for the Wanderer's gift of noticing = 7). Squinting works: the white light resolves into a slow-turning ring of pale fire, a doorway on its edge, and beneath it the plain swirls like water draining toward it. The cost: the focused noticing is itself a kind of magic and costs 5 mana, and an asteroid slams down in the distance and throws a shockwave of blue rings racing toward the Wanderer. The beacon's attention ticks as the rings carry the impact to its feet. The Wanderer is shaken but unharmed, and the beacon still does not draw nearer. The swirling floor suggests it is pulling them in, not receding. A main quest awakens: find out what the light is waiting for.
announce: Quest begun: The Waiting Light. The Beacon's Gaze ticks: 2/6

roll.presentation: Three slow pulses of the beacon counted like a heartbeat, each one a die, summing to a partial answer
roll.reason: Can the Wanderer pierce the distance to see what the light truly is, without drawing the beacon's notice?

objectives.text: Learn what the white light is waiting for
Reach the ring of fire at the horizon
Survive the shockwave of the falling asteroid

narration: You squint, and the world leans closer. The white light unfolds into a ring of pale fire, taller than a cathedral and turning slowly on its edge, a doorway with no wall around it. Beneath you the plain begins to swirl, black glass drawing into long spirals that run toward the ring. It is not receding. It is pulling you in. The focus costs you, a cold ache behind the eyes as your mana thins. Then a streak of orange tears the sky far to the east and an asteroid slams into the plain. A shockwave of blue rings races across the glass toward the doorway's feet, and the ring answers with a single slow pulse, as though it has just learned your name.

facts.description: What looked like a lantern is a vast ring of pale white fire, about 60 m tall, standing on its edge and turning slowly like a wheel. Its interior is a bright, still white void, and it pulses once in a slow rhythm. A long bright reflection runs down the glass toward the Wanderer.
facts.placement: About 2 km due north of the Wanderer, standing on the horizon of obsidian_plain.

facts.description: The obsidian surface flows in wide slow spirals of dark glass and pale mist, like water draining into a basin. The spiral arms run north toward the fire ring and glint with silver veins.
facts.placement: On obsidian_plain, spanning from 100 m north of the Wanderer to the base of northern_light.

facts.description: A jagged black-and-ember asteroid, about 15 m across, is half buried in the glass, glowing dull orange at its cracks and trailing smoke. Fractured glass radiates from it in a starburst about 80 m wide.
facts.placement: About 600 m east and 1.2 km north of the Wanderer, on obsidian_plain.

facts.description: Wide bands of bright blue light race across the plain as a ripple from the impact, each ring a few meters thick and brighter than the watching rings. They sweep toward the base of the fire ring.
facts.placement: On obsidian_plain, radiating from asteroid_crater and passing north-west toward northern_light.

notes: The white light is now a 60 m ring of pale fire turning on the horizon, with a black-glass spiral draining toward it. A glowing asteroid sits in its cracked starburst far to the east, with bright blue shockwave bands sweeping out from it.

critique: The beacon still reads as a bright dot with a soft glow, not a 60 m ring of pale fire. The plain is a flat black void with no spirals or crater visible, and the cape is a clean wedge. Shockwave rings are barely visible, and the horizon is a hard line. I'm steering toward a luminous ring doorway, visible spiral arms of silver mist, and a glowing ember crater far off, all reflected in the glass.

suggestions.change: Make the ring legible: set torus tube 2.2 to 1.6 and R 30, add a second thinner torus (R 33, tube 0.5, #bcd4ff) counter-rotating, make the inner disc a radial gradient (center #ffffff, edge #9fc0ff, opacity 0.8), and add a soft halo sprite of radius 90 m (#cfe0ff, opacity 0.35). Tilt the wheel about 25° on y so the ring shows an ellipse, not a dot. Add a slow pulse of scale 1 to 1.04 every 6 s.

Make spirals visible: raise opacity 0.3 to 0.55, color #9fb4e0, sharper arms (pow 3 instead of 6), 5 arms, and shrink size s to 2400 so the arms are denser. Add a rotation speed of 0.03. Add a second mist layer at y 0.3, color #4a5a85, opacity 0.15, drifting, so arms read as streaming mist.

Make it a glowing landmark: raise emissiveIntensity 0.35 to 1.2 with bright #ff6a20 cracks, add a point-like glow sprite 120 m (#ff7a30, opacity 0.5), a rising smoke column 150 m tall (dark #1a1418 billboards, opacity 0.4) and an ember reflection streak on the glass 300 m long (#ff8a40). Scale starburst to 160 m.

Add a horizon haze band: set skyBottom #3a5588, fogColor #22366a, fogDensity 0.00018, exposure 1.0, bloom 0.9. Add a distant faint mountain silhouette ring at 6 km, color #0a1224, height 150-400 m with noise, fading into fog, to break the hard horizon line.

styleGuide: Palette: obsidian #05070d, midnight indigo #1c2a4a, horizon blue #3a5588, ripple blue #7fb8ff, beacon white #e6efff, cape navy #0c1534, silver thread #bcd4ff, ember #ff6a20. Mood: cold, silent, vast night with one lone light and one warm wound. Lighting: low moonlike fill, luminous horizon haze, mirror reflections, bloom on highlights only. Materials: polished black glass, roughness under 0.05; cloth with soft sheen; emissive thread; glowing ember cracks. Realism: high, smooth gradients, no flat grey. Motifs: converging rings, spiral mist arms, long reflection path north, scale through emptiness.
unlockReason: Content is at 97% of its byte budget, so I can't add the crater smoke, mountain silhouettes and richer ring detail. More bytes and a second light would let the ring and the ember glow cast real light onto the glass.

message: Unlock declined: the next tier opens in 4 turns.

notes: I made the beacon a tilted double ring with a gradient disc and a wide halo, and I made the mist spirals denser and brighter. The crater now glows hotter with an ember halo and a wider starburst, and I added horizon haze. The memory budget was too tight for the smoke column, ember streak, second mist layer and mountain ring, so I left those out.
